thread: Mira: heads up — onboarding run for `falcon-lite-q4_0` tomorrow. want to lock down SLOs for funcall/json acceptance before we flip canary. Sam: thanks, Mira. what SLOs are we proposing? parse success, latency P95, and downstream tool error rate? Mira: yeah. rough draft: - parse_success >= 99.0% (schema strict) - funcall_latency_p95 <= 250ms - tool_error_rate <= 0.5% (after retries) Devin: pinging the canary plan: we run 1k requests over a variety of prompts, 70% single-tool, 30% multi-tool. retries enabled: budget 2, backoff 200ms. Lucy: can we add a parse_repair_rate metric? we want to measure cases where we run `json-repair` fallback and still get usable output. Mira: good call. add parse_repair_rate <= 1.5% and repair_success >= 80%. Rajesh: sg. also need to capture soft-failures where model emits trailing garbage after valid JSON — treat as parse_failure unless rescue strips suffix. Sam: for canary automation, i'll add these as assertions in the runbook. sample check block: ``` assert metrics.parse_success >= 0.99 assert metrics.funcall_latency.p95 <= 0.25 assert metrics.tool_error_rate <= 0.005 ``` Sam: run command will be: `/canary run falcon-lite-q4_0 --suite json-funcall-slo --samples 1000 --retries 2` canary-bot: starting canary run falcon-lite-q4_0 · suite=json-funcall-slo · samples=1000 · retries=2 canary-bot: progress 200/1000 · parse_success=0.986 · p95_latency=0.29s · tool_error_rate=0.007 :warning: Lucy: hitting the first threshold failure on parse_success and latency. any known regression compared to baseline? Devin: baseline (raven-v2-q4) numbers for same suite: parse_success=0.995, p95_latency=0.21s, tool_error_rate=0.003 Mira: that's significant. let's capture a small batch of failing traces and inspect heuristics (suffixes, stray commas, non-utf8 bytes). Sam: exported 150 failing traces to `/tmp/falcon_onboard/failures-2026-03-21.ndjson` — includes model output + parsed attempted repair steps. Rajesh: quick diff: new model emits `]` on same line as `` sometimes, plus occasional `�` in stream. likely tokenization/encoder mismatch in quant path. Lucy: can we test with `strip_control_chars=true` and `enforce_json_wrapper=true` to see delta? Devin: re-run 200 sample with those options: `/canary run ... --samples 200 --opts strip_control_chars,enforce_json_wrapper` canary-bot: quick re-run 200 · parse_success=0.992 · p95_latency=0.26s · tool_error_rate=0.004 :thumbsup: Mira: improvement but still shy on latency. P95 moved from 0.29s -> 0.26s, good on parse. what's the cost hit? Sam: latency increases ~20ms median due to wrapper postprocess. cost negligible for canary but needs perf review for production. Rajesh: hypothesis: quantized kv-cache alignment causing extra decoding tokens -> slower generation tail (function closing tokens). need a micro-bench on kv-prefix lengths. Lucy: propose acceptance gates for rollout: - soft gate: allow parse_repair up to 1.5% with human review on samples - hard gate: parse_success >= 99.0 AND p95_latency <= 0.27s - rollback if tool_error_rate > 0.006 Mira: +1 to that. also add monitoring alert rule to escalate if parse_repair_rate spikes >2% in 1h window. Sam: I'll post runbook snippet to the onboarding wiki and schedule a short triage tomorrow 10:30am to decide final flag. Lucy: one more ask — add a targeted eval with multi-tool nested calls (2+ sequential funcalls) to ensure KV cache ordering doesn't reorder tool intents. Devin: noted. adding nested-tool stress sample 200 requests. canary-bot: final aggregated summary · samples=1000 · parse_success=0.993 · p95_latency=0.255s · tool_error_rate=0.0042 · parse_repair_rate=0.9% · repair_success=82% · status=conditional-pass Mira: thanks team. conditional-pass -> proceed to staged rollout behind `json-strict=false` for 10% traffic and tight monitoring. we'll revisit in 72h. Sam: I'll open PR for rollout flags and the runbook with exact thresholds + commands. linking it here when ready. :rocket: Rajesh: dropping a checklist item: schedule quant micro-bench on 4 GPU types next week. Lucy: thanks — great work. :clap:
